research_objective: Evaluate whether and how different document chunking strategies affect retrieval performance in educational RAG question answering.

key_findings.finding: Heading-based and Paragraph-based strategies consistently showed higher observed retrieval performance than arbitrary character-based strategies across all metrics.
The omnibus tests provide evidence against the null hypothesis of no difference across strategies for all four metrics (Friedman p < 0.001).

Heading-based produced higher observed values than Fixed-size, with statistically significant paired differences across all evaluated metrics. Fixed-size and Recursive Character chunking showed no significant differences from each other.

The Friedman effect-size estimates increased from Recall@1 through Recall@5, indicating that the degree of between-strategy rank differentiation observed in this dataset was larger at higher retrieval cutoffs.

structural_interpretation.finding: The observed pattern is consistent with the possibility that preserving document-level discourse boundaries affects retrieval matching.

limitations: Restricted to Chapters 1-5 of a single educational textbook.
Small dataset of 50 manually curated questions.
Fixed embedding model and static retrieval configuration (top_k=5, cosine similarity).
Evaluation focuses strictly on retrieval success (Recall/MRR) without end-to-end LLM generation evaluation.
Provenance-derived evaluation may penalize strategies that find correct alternative source text.
future_work: End-to-end evaluation of generated answer quality.
Testing with advanced retrieval architectures such as neural reranking and hybrid search.
